meta.title: ky - tiny HTTP client over Fetch

summary: ky is a small HTTP client library built on top of the Fetch API, exporting a default instance plus named exports for errors and type guards.
The public entry point source/index.ts builds instances through createInstance and validates/merges options via source/utils/merge.ts before constructing a Ky object.
source/core/Ky.ts contains the Ky class whose static create() runs init hooks, constructs the instance, and returns a ResponsePromise with body shortcuts like json() and bytes().
A request flows through #run(): beforeRequest hooks, then #retry()/#fetch() which calls the configured fetch, then afterResponse hooks, with retries and beforeRetry hooks on failure.
Retries are orchestrated in #retryFromError, which consults retry options, calculates delays (with jitter and Retry-After style timing headers), waits via source/utils/delay.ts, and re-runs fetch.
Errors are typed (HTTPError, NetworkError, TimeoutError, etc.) in source/errors, and response bodies can be limited by size and streamed with progress callbacks.
The library feature-detects capabilities such as request/response streams, abort signals, and FormData at import time in source/core/constants.ts.
It targets both browsers and Node.js 22+, delegating actual network I/O to the global or configured fetch function.

flow.title: Call ky(url, options)
flow.text: User calls the default instance; createInstance builds a getOptions closure that validates and merges defaults with per-call options.

flow.title: Create request
flow.text: createRequest calls Ky.create(input, getOptions()) inside a try, so setup errors reject the returned ResponsePromise.

flow.title: Ky.create
flow.text: Runs init hooks, constructs a Ky instance, and returns an async ResponsePromise whose body shortcuts (json, bytes, etc.) are attached.

flow.title: Run request
flow.text: #run awaits beforeRequest hooks; if one returns a Response it is used directly, otherwise #retry is invoked.

flow.title: Fetch
flow.text: #fetch clones the request for possible retries, then calls the configured fetch (or timeout wrapper) and records the original request.

flow.title: After response
flow.text: #run runs afterResponse hooks; on non-ok status it builds an HTTPError and may call #retryFromError for another attempt.

flow.title: Retry delay
flow.text: #retryFromError calculates delay, waits with delay(), runs beforeRetry hooks, then calls #retry again.

flow.title: Result
flow.text: The awaited ResponsePromise resolves with the final Response (or rejects with a typed error), and body methods read/parse the body.

interview.pitch: I worked on ky, a tiny HTTP client built on the Fetch API. The public API in source/index.ts creates instances and method shorthands like get and post, delegating to the Ky class in source/core/Ky.ts. A call runs through Ky.create, which executes init hooks, builds normalized options via merge utilities, and returns a ResponsePromise with body shortcuts. The core #run method orchestrates beforeRequest hooks, the actual fetch through #fetch, afterResponse hooks, and retries via #retryFromError, including delays, beforeRetry hooks, and typed errors. It leans on feature detection in constants.ts and streams bodies with size limits and progress callbacks.
tradeoffs: Retries clone the request body up front, which can buffer large uploads in memory; cloning is skipped when retries are disabled to avoid this.
Body shortcuts like json() are attached to the same promise, so reading happens after dispatch and must handle undefined responses from ky.stop.
Hook errors and timeouts are funneled into beforeError where possible, which keeps one error channel but complicates control flow.
Response size limiting and progress reporting rely on ReadableStream support, so older runtimes without streams cannot use those features.
The managed abort signal and clone bookkeeping add complexity to support timeouts, retries, and user aborts together.

questions.q: How does a single request flow through ky?
questions.a: Ky.create runs init hooks, builds the instance, and returns a ResponsePromise. #run calls beforeRequest hooks, then #retry/#fetch to perform the network call, then afterResponse hooks, retrying via #retryFromError on failure.
#calculateRetryDelay checks retry limit, method allowlist, shouldRetry, timeout, HTTP status codes, and network errors, and supports forced retries from afterResponse hooks via ForceRetryError.
Per-request timeout wraps fetch in source/utils/timeout.ts with setTimeout and AbortController; totalTimeout is tracked separately against a deadline in Ky.

Hooks are merged in source/utils/merge.ts and run in order; beforeRequest can replace the request or return a Response, afterResponse can modify or force a retry, beforeRetry can change request/options or stop.

questions.q: How is the request body handled for retries?
questions.a: #fetch clones the request only when retries are enabled, assigns the clone to this.request for later attempts, and cancels unused bodies to avoid leaks.
Typed errors HTTPError, NetworkError, TimeoutError, ResponseSizeError, SchemaValidationError, and ForceRetryError, re-exported from source/index.ts.

questions.q: How does ky support streaming and progress?
questions.a: Feature detection in constants.ts gates stream support; body.ts streams request/response bodies and enforces maxResponseSize, and onDownloadProgress wraps responses.

The Ky class orchestrates hooks, fetch, retries, timeouts, and response decoration.

Module map
Entry Point (source): creates and exports the default ky instance and method shorthands, plus create/extend factories.
Core Engine (source/core): Ky class orchestrating hooks, fetch, retries, timeouts, and response decoration.
Constants (source/core): feature detection, supported methods, response types, and retry markers.
Retry Timing (source/core): parses Retry-After style headers to compute server-provided retry delays.
Options Merge (source/utils): validates and deeply merges defaults and per-call options, headers, hooks, and search params.
Normalize (source/utils): normalizes request method, retry method, and retry options.
Body Utilities (source/utils): cancels unused bodies, streams request/response bodies, and enforces response size limits.
Errors (source/errors): typed error classes for HTTP, network, timeout, response size, and schema validation failures.
Types (source/types): TypeScript definitions for options, hooks, retry, request, response, and ResponsePromise.
Utilities (source/utils): timeout, delay, type guards, and network-error detection helpers.
Fetch API (global fetch): underlying network transport invoked by Ky#fetch via global or configured fetch.

Request path
1. User calls the default instance; createInstance builds a getOptions closure that validates and merges defaults with per-call options.
2. createRequest calls Ky.create(input, getOptions()) inside a try, so setup errors reject the returned ResponsePromise.
3. Ky.create runs init hooks, constructs a Ky instance, and returns an async ResponsePromise whose body shortcuts are attached.
4. #run awaits beforeRequest hooks; if one returns a Response it is used directly, otherwise #retry is invoked.
5. #fetch clones the request for possible retries, then calls the configured fetch or timeout wrapper and records the original request.
6. #run runs afterResponse hooks; on non-ok status it builds an HTTPError and may call #retryFromError for another attempt.
7. #retryFromError calculates delay, waits with delay(), runs beforeRetry hooks, then calls #retry again.
8. The awaited ResponsePromise resolves with the final Response or rejects with a typed error, and body methods read/parse the body.

Rules
New instance construction and exports belong in the Entry Point at source/index.ts, which imports Ky and merge utilities.
Option validation and merging belong in source/utils/merge.ts; method, retry method, and retry option normalization belong in source/utils/normalize.ts.
Retry orchestration and retry decisions belong in Core Engine at source/core/Ky.ts; server-provided retry delay parsing belongs in source/core/retry-timing.ts, and waiting belongs in source/utils/delay.ts.
Body cancellation, streaming, and response size limits belong in source/utils/body.ts; capability gating belongs in source/core/constants.ts.
Typed errors are defined in source/errors and re-exported by the Entry Point.
Network I/O must go through the configured or global fetch invoked by Core Engine, with timeout handling delegated to source/utils/timeout.ts.
Hooks are merged in source/utils/merge.ts and run by Core Engine; beforeRequest may replace the request or return a Response, afterResponse may modify or force a retry, and beforeRetry may change request/options or stop.

External services
Fetch API (global or configured fetch): underlying network transport invoked by Ky#fetch; owned by the Fetch API module and called by Core Engine.

Known weak spots
Retries clone the request body up front, which can buffer large uploads in memory; cloning is skipped when retries are disabled to avoid this.
Body shortcuts such as json() are attached to the same promise, so reading happens after dispatch and must handle undefined responses from ky.stop.
Hook errors and timeouts are funneled into beforeError where possible, which keeps one error channel but complicates control flow.
Response size limiting and progress reporting rely on ReadableStream support, so runtimes without streams cannot use those features.
The managed abort signal and clone bookkeeping add complexity to supporting timeouts, retries, and user aborts together.
